card.title: Kinetic energy
card.says: the energy a body has because it is moving: proportional to mass $m$ and to the **square** of its speed $v$, so doubling the speed **quadruples** $E_k$.
card.from: the work-energy theorem: accelerating mass $m$ from rest with net force $F = ma$ over $\Delta x = \dfrac{v^2}{2a}$ does work $W = F \Delta x = \dfrac{1}{2} m v^2$.
card.useWhen: a moving object speeds up, slows down, or trades speed for height or spring compression—especially when you do not need time.
card.example: A $2\text{ kg}$ ball at $v = 6\text{ m/s}$ has $E_k = \dfrac{1}{2}(2)(6^2) = 36\text{ J}$. At $v = 12\text{ m/s}$ (twice as fast), $E_k = \dfrac{1}{2}(2)(12^2) = 144\text{ J}$ — four times as much.
card.analogy: A car's braking distance grows fourfold when you double your speed because the brakes must absorb four times the kinetic energy.
